title: Philo Vance
paragraphs: A sophisticated detective series based on S. S. Van Dine's amateur sleuth Philo Vance, who applies observation, psychology, and deduction to complex murder cases.

Radio detective adaptations of S. S. Van Dine’s Philo Vance character. Frozen GRH snapshot contains a 1943 audition precursor, two 1945 archive recordings, and 92 Ziv-era recordings through July 1950.

GRH documents the program through 1943 audition precursor (April 29, 1943 to April 29, 1943), NBC José Ferrer run (July 5, 1945 to September 27, 1945) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], ABC West John Emery run (July 23, 1946 to 1946) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and Frederick Ziv syndicated run (July 13, 1948 to July 4, 1950).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Frederick W. Ziv (producer on 58 recordings), Henry Sylvern (organist on 56 recordings and organ on 2 recordings), [[person|jackson-beck|Jackson Beck]] (performer on 58 recordings), Jeanne K. Harrison (director on 58 recordings), S. S. Van Dine (creator on 58 recordings), Joan Alexander (performer on 57 recordings), and George Petrie (performer on 11 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.070a5b7dde24b155|Ziv]] (syndicated by), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include deductive investigation, murder investigation, inheritance and wealth, art and valuable objects, theater and performance world, and police and prosecution.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including S. S. Van Dine literary detective origin, Network summer-replacement detective drama, Postwar syndicated detective production, and Armchair-detective clue structure.
